title: Executive sync runbook + open asks
content:
Purpose: quick personal runbook for the weekly exec staff sync. Keep the meeting tight (45m), land decisions and owners, surface any risk of rollback for Dedicated rollout, and capture follow-ups as action items.

Topline elevator: we are stable on hosted but Dedicated capacity needs 2 quick fixes (autoscaler tuning, backup fallback routing) to avoid churn on new contracts. Forecast still positive: Q4 usage +21% MoM but unit cost ticked up ~4% due to small-SS batching regression.

Meeting constraints / goals:
- Duration: 45 minutes total.
- Outcomes: 1) Decision on Dedicated autoscaler change (canary), 2) Approval for small-funded A/B of new batching patch to 10% of traffic, 3) Query to CFO about short-term budget for transient GPU burst.

Suggested agenda (45m):
- 0:00–0:05 quick wins and blockers (me) — 3 bullets
- 0:05–0:15 metrics spotlight (Ops) — P50/P95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, Dedicated pool utilization
- 0:15–0:25 Dedicated rollout status + incident follow-ups (Infra lead) — decision point
- 0:25–0:35 Product / GTM asks (Product lead) — customer escalations, contract SLAs
- 0:35–0:43 Risks & mitigation + decision capture (SRE/Head of Eng)
- 0:43–0:45 Parking lot / quick next-steps + owner assignment

Three metrics to call out (prep notes):
1) P50 token latency (hosted api): 72ms — target 65ms. Root cause: small input batching regression after patch 2024-11-02.
2) Unit cost (hosted, per 1k tokens) — $0.62 now vs target $0.55. Impact mainly on long-tail chat sessions; potential to tune quantization policy for non-critical models.
3) Dedicated utilization — 84% avg, spikes to 97% on M/W peak windows. If spikes persist, SLA risk for new enterprise contracts.

Incident summary (brief):
- 2024-11-12 — brief degradation on shard a3-14 during spike; auto-fallback worked but latency spiked. Postmortem draft: infra/incident-20241112-draft.
- Immediate ask: enable fallback pool (warm) for critical enterprise routes for 48 hours while we patch autoscaler.

Decisions required (frame why):
A) Autoscaler canary: tune aggressiveness to recover from microspikes. Ops recommends a cautious canary (2 pools, 2 days).
  - Pros: reduces latency spikes, buys time.
  - Cons: slightly higher cost while warm.
B) Short A/B for batching patch: 10% of production traffic for 72 hours. Data needed: latency & cost delta vs control.
  - If latency <= 5% worse and cost <= 2% higher, approve full rollout.
C) Temporary GPU burst budget of $40k for next 30 days for enterprise onboarding (ask CFO).

Who to ask to bring what (prep):
- Benji: one-slide heatmap for Dedicated pool utilization + quick table of contracts at risk. (Slack: #infra, PR linked).
- Sofia: customer escalation list with top 3 accounts and SLA language we promised.
- Priya (SRE): short summary of fallback behavior and expected residual risk if we enable warm pool.
- Finance: short note from CFO or head of finance on flexibility for 30-day burst.

Open asks / action tracker (capture during meeting) — template I'll fill live: (format: ASK — owner — due)
- Enable warm fallback for enterprise routes — Benji — 2024-11-21
- Start 10% A/B for batching patch — Priya — 2024-11-22
- Finance approval for $40k burst — CFO (TBD) — 2024-11-24
- Customer comms draft for impacted enterprise customers — Sofia — 2024-11-22

Notes-to-self / talking beats:
- Lead with empathy on customer impact, then show data quickly. Avoid long engineering deep dives.
- Use the canary as a safety valve; frame it as risk-reduction, not cost-cut.
- If CFO pushes back, propose a scoping ramp: $20k initial + review in 10 days.
- Keep ask for batching A/B narrowly scoped: 10% only on non-critical models; blacklist enterprise routes.

Possible pushback (prep answers):
- "Cost too high": offer phased approach, highlight avoided churn % (if we lose 1 enterprise account, revenue impact > burst).
- "Need data": commit to 72hr A/B and share a readout in 5 working days.

Parking lot items (non-blocking):
- Explore quantization profile for chat-small models (optimize cost in Q1).
- Follow-up: evaluate edge routing policy for APAC region (latency improvements).

Script for opening (2–3 sentences):
"Quick update: core product is stable, but we saw a small batching regression that nudged unit cost. Dedicated utilization is healthy but some pools are tight — I have 3 narrowly scoped asks to keep us out of churn and preserve runway for new enterprise deals. I’ll be brief and mark owners/duedates live."

Post-meeting follow-up steps (my checklist):
- Capture action items in exec tracker (confluence) — <after meeting> — Claire
- Ping owners in Slack with 1-line summary + due date — Claire -> #exec-actions
- Draft short external note for affected customers if Sofia asks for it — Claire/Sofia
- Sync with Benji for rollout timeline and verify the autoscaler canary config — Claire/Benji

Random scratch reminders (personal):
- Bring the one-pager on model quantization economics — might be useful if cost discussion goes technical.
- Keep tempo: interruptions > defer to parking lot.
- Remember to call out success metrics for the canary (latency delta, error rate, cost delta).

End of runbook. I'll paste the action-tracker template into confluence after the call and tag owners.

-- Claire
